1514925971723411457 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 142 🔁 18
“Doing stuff” is inherently an optimistic activity

to START doing stuff, you have to have *some* kind of inkling that it could go well,

And to KEEP doing stuff, you need to cultivate that inkling and prune away the constant assault of pessimisms, both internal and external
↓
1514926363786063874 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 39 🔁 3
there’s a feedback loop, where when you get away from pessimism juuuuuust enough to stop complaining about how nothing will ever work,

And you get enough space to make *some* attempt to make it work,

more optimism has to come in. It’s sink or swim.
↓
1514926858915266563 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 33
& more pessimism has to get dealt with. You have to get better at recognizing
“yes, all this stuff could go wrong.
Yes, even if it goes right, there are problems w it.
No, it’s not going to be perfect.
Yes, I’m wide-open exposed to criticism on all of this,
But I can still do it”
↓
1514927756999634944 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 26 🔁 1
Looking at my old journals, old articles, and looking at people who remind me really strongly of myself a couple years ago,

I see this really thick layer of pessimism that was so comforting.
↓
1514928328096075783 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 31
I could wrap myself up in a nice cozy blanket of pessimism, running through all the problems with what other people were doing, the ways their attempts were flawed, the ways things would go wrong even if those problems were addressed, how unworkable everything is,
↓
1514928696313978882 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 29
mmmm.  
cozy.  
No need to try anything.
And no need to feel inferior to the people who are trying things.
cuz they’ll either fail, or sell their souls to succeed.
Much better to recognize its all fucked,
and then just marinate in the fuckedness.
Mmm.
that’s the stuff.
↓
1514928965751877637 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 33 🔁 1
Marinate in the fuckedness.
the womblike fuckedness of total unworkability.
↓
1514929206832111616 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 25 🔁 1
Trying Things and Doing Things, on the other hand—

Feels incredibly exposed and unstable a lot of the time.
↓
1514929762397003776 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 15
It’s not like that voice that recognizes all the problems and difficulties evaporates and goes away. It’s still there, advising on ways to try harder, fail better and so on,
↓
1514929763894407181 [2022-04-15] @the_wilderless 💜 20 🔁 1
But now I can’t marinate in the pessimism, I have to be its coworker, listening to all its complaints and assessing which ones can be addressed and which ones I just have to say a prayer on and hope they go fine
↓

1515315162248531976 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 16
More and more often lately, I’ve been in a position of trying to find a neat, clear, succinct way of answering questions like
“What is an *image?” And 
“why should I care about *image work?”

It’s giving me a lot of sympathy for the first rounds of meditation teachers in the west
↓
1515315164131872777 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 10
We kinda take for granted nowadays that everyone knows what meditation is, and has some basic handle on a few reasons someone might want to do it.

I am astounded by the amount of cultural infrastructure that has gone into that.
↓
1515315558983548938 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 9
You say words like Meditation, Mindfulness, Zen—anything in that family—and people have entire knowledge-complexes available to them around those syllables.
We can quibble about how accurate or wholesome some of those complexes are, but they’re *there,* people know how to engage
↓
1515315560632000518 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 9
People know where to go for different styles of meditation, which styles they vibe with and which ones they don't,

The know the type of people to seek out for help or alternate viewpoints or a bit of perspective—all of this is built-in to the word “meditation,” usually
↓
1515315973733163011 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 9
And it wasn’t always like that.

Can you imagine being one of the people who had to try to explain to Americans 80 years ago what meditation is, and why they might want to check it out?
↓
1515316453481848844 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 8
“so I just sit still?
What do you mean focus on my breathing? I breathe perfectly fine without focusing on it, thank you v much.
It’s about cultivating an experience? Is that experience more fun than watching tv, or playing catch w my kids?
What do you mean it’s ‘not about fun’?”
↓
1515317017418641413 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 9
You could try to explain that it will transform their minds and their lives if they try it,

But honestly, *every* product says that. Just this week I’ve heard that about like 20 different things from infrared saunas to hiking to productivity apps. Why listen to this one?
↓
1515325602508812297 [2022-04-16] @the_wilderless 💜 4

Which, I’m not complaining. Just noting the task here.

For everyone else:
The aim of this project is to a) develop and b) communicate the type of imaginal work I do,
a type of work that follows from Carl Jung, James Hillman, Rob Burbea, Robert Moss,,,
(+ a bunch of esoteric shit I’ve dabbled with over the years 🙃)
├── 1517936965383081986 [2022-04-23] @regencrypto 💜 2
│   @the_wilderless is this the new thing? 🙌🥰
└── 1517937595942158336 [2022-04-23] @the_wilderless 💜 1
    ‼️ The most important part, to me, and to the future of the work, is a) developing.
    
    Developing it mostly takes the form of a lot of practice, a lot of reading, a lot of journaling, and a lot of discussing what I’ve practiced, read, and journaled on https://t.co/EdPvSCX3Fc
      [Quoting @the_wilderless: There's at least a 30-item list I could put right here, but I backspaced all that to focus on the ones I'm most interested in at the moment: work like Coherence Therapy, Alexander Technique, Kastrup, McGilchrist, (more) Hillman, narrative, creative energy, art…]
    ↓
    1517937598412607488 [2022-04-23] @the_wilderless 💜 1
    It takes time and effort and focus—and leaves very little by way of tangible things I can point at. (Or at least it doesn’t *reliably* lead to tangibles.)
    
    It’s vital, but it’s very much a long-game move
    ↓
    1517938543758393344 [2022-04-23] @the_wilderless 
    ❗️Also important is b) communication.
    
    The main plans in this area involve 
    -writing articles that put the imaginal in context—both historical context and practical context
    -building workshops for particular applications of imaginal practice
    ↓
    1517938545406656514 [2022-04-23] @the_wilderless 💜 1
    -writing a manifesto on Active Worlding (and facilitating a manifesto-writing quasi-nanowrimo for anyone else who’s got a manifesto brewing 🧐)
    -and hopefully getting a better website up and running

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand is a **Patron-Funded Creative Sabbatical** centered on River Kenna (@the_wilderless) receiving a microgrant from Brent Baum in April 2022 to develop 'imaginal practice'—a synthesis of Jungian active imagination, somatic work, and spiritual exploration. The boundary object is the grant itself (initially ~$2500 for 3 months) and River's public articulation of goals. The arc moves from Aspiration (River's dream of a grant in Feb 2022) → Catalyst (Brent's call for community funding) → Execution (River completing 6/7 goals despite mental health crises) → Retrospective validation (Sept 2022). This is **constructive rather than dialectical**—the community rallies around a shared member rather than debating the work's merit. Evolution is medium (River produces workshops, a manifesto, a website), but the *idea* of imaginal practice itself doesn't significantly evolve through discourse—it's more a **documentation of one person's funded creative process**. Cohesion is high within a small donor circle. Utility is low for outsiders (no accessible artifacts explaining 'what imaginal practice is'), though potentially high for the niche community if River's future work delivers on the promise.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Catalyst: Brent Baum announces intention to fund community projects, names River as first grantee, inviting others to join
River's immediate validation: 'This belongs here ✨'—accepting the grant and signaling alignment with community funding ethos
Pre-launch framing: River articulates the core tension of 'Doing Stuff'—optimism vs pessimism, exposure vs marinating in critique
The Announcement: River details the 3-part project (Communication, Exploration, Practice) and timeline starting May 1
Study Roadmap: River lists the intellectual territory (Coherence Therapy, Alexander Technique, McGilchrist, Hillman) signaling ambition
Funding tiers: River transparently breaks down what's possible with minimum viable ($2500/3mo) vs extended runway
Cross-pollination vision: River identifies potential allies (psychedelics, web3, meditation, narrative) showing ecosystem awareness
Manifesto framing: 'Let a thousand gorgeous weirdnesses bloom'—the imaginal as source of necessary strangeness/fate
The Retrospective (4 months later): River reports completing 6/7 goals despite ADHD discovery and mental health crisis
Closing the loop: River connects back to the original Feb 2022 dream-grant, validating the manifestation process

title: A $2.5k Twitter microgrant turns into “imaginal” sabbatical
summary:
Brent Baum basically points at River Kenna (@the_wilderless) and says “this corner of twitter is special—let’s fund our own,” and within days it’s a live-fire experiment in patronage: can a few people scraping together ~$2.5k buy someone three months of creative runway? River treats it like a real sabbatical, not a tip jar—transparent tiers, deliverables, and a whole vibe of *stop marinating in pessimism and actually do the thing*.

Arc is clean: **trigger** = @_brentbaum’s April 9 “I want to write microgrants” call (“healing, art, and community” / “milestones, not marathons,” plus the semi-joke about a “secret cartel of tpot folks” funding projects). **Peak** = late April fundraising sprint where Brent posts “we’re only a few hundred dollars off,” and River sells the work hard: imaginal practice as Jung/Hillman/Burbea-adjacent “esoteric shit,” with the pitch that more runway buys not just output but safety for deep practice (“if I strike upon a dense bit of shadow… it won’t endanger deliverables”). He drops the whole ecosystem map—“CROSS-POLLINATORS” like psychedelics, web3/solarpunk, meditation, narrative, astrology—and coins the rallying cry “Let a thousand gorgeous weirdnesses bloom,” including the etymology bit where “weird” means *fateful*, not just quirky.

**Outcome/current state** = September check-in: River says the schedule got “wonky,” the funding ended up “a hair under the minimum,” and yet he hit **6 of 7** goals—while a potato diet “precipitated… one of the more intense mental health crises” of his adult life and he realized he likely has ADHD (shoutout @rosaclewis stepping in as informal project manager). Tangibles: a Somatic Resonance workshop, a manifesto/vision doc, more allies, and a new website—while the one big miss is the grand contextual essay explaining imaginal practice as a culmination of 20th-century spirituality (“bigger task than I thought”). The residue is the meme/operating model: tiny patron microgrants + radical transparency about runway tiers + “weirdness” as destiny-coded creative fuel—useful if you’re in that Twitter micro-scene trying to bootstrap art/healing work without waiting for institutions to notice you.
